session.title: 20-minute full-body strength session

exercises.name: Calf Raise — Density Beginner
how: Stand tall with light support nearby. Rise onto the balls of your feet, pause at the top, then lower your heels slowly all the way down.
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
form_cues: What it should feel like: calves working through a full, controlled range
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
What it should not feel like: ankle pain or bouncing through the reps
safety_cues: What it should not feel like: ankle pain or bouncing through the reps
regressions: Use both hands for support and a smaller range.
progressions: Use one leg at a time or hold a dumbbell.

visual.alt_text: Calf Raise — Density Beginner: start position, controlled movement and finish position shown as a three-state coaching sequence.

purpose.benefit: Works the lower-leg muscles used when pushing off the ground during walking and climbing steps.
purpose.weightLoss: Strength work helps build and maintain muscle as part of a balanced activity routine. Weight loss depends on your overall activity and energy intake over time.

exercises.selection_reason: Included for strength within your selected 20-minute home session. It needs no exercise equipment.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge — Easy Day Beginner
how: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Brace gently, drive through your heels and lift your hips until shoulders, hips and knees form a long line; lower slowly.
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
form_cues: What it should feel like: glutes squeezing hard at the top
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
What it should not feel like: cramping in the lower back or hamstrings taking over completely
safety_cues: What it should not feel like: cramping in the lower back or hamstrings taking over completely
regressions: Lift only as high as you can keep the ribs down and glutes working.
progressions: Pause for two seconds at the top or progress to a single-leg-supported version.

exercises.name: Chest Press — Endurance Beginner
how: Lie supported with a dumbbell in each hand, elbows slightly below shoulder level. Press the weights up until your arms are long without smashing the dumbbells together, then lower with control.
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
form_cues: What it should feel like: chest and triceps working with shoulders staying settled
Keep it controlled enough that you could stop the rep cleanly at any point.
What it should not feel like: pain at the front of the shoulder or excessive back arch
safety_cues: What it should not feel like: pain at the front of the shoulder or excessive back arch
regressions: Use lighter weights or a neutral grip.
progressions: Increase the load a little once every rep stays smooth.

exercises.name: Row — Gym Beginner

safety_cues: What it should not feel like: twisting through the torso or shoulder pinching

progressions: Increase the weight or add a short squeeze at the top.
